more_info.overview: Carmoisine, also called azorubine, is a red azo food colour. Food-grade material consists mainly of colouring salts. It gives foods red to maroon shades. The specified material is supplied as red powder or granules.
more_info.origin: A synthetic azo dye, generally supplied as its sodium salt.
more_info.daily_intake: 4 mg/kg body weight per day (EFSA, 2009), retained in the 2015 exposure assessment.
more_info.side_effects:
At reported food uses, EFSA's refined 2015 exposure estimates were below the ADI. Limited evidence did not establish this individual colour as a cause of intolerance reactions or behavioural effects reported for mixtures.
A model using maximum permitted levels estimated that some high-consuming toddlers and children could exceed the ADI. This is an intake estimate, not an observed clinical effect.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; unripened cheese excluding products falling in category 16.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
